tagline: Along Crowley’s Ridge, two lakes and views into river valleys
intro: The St. Francis Scenic Byway follows the crest of Crowley’s Ridge for over 21 miles between Marianna and Helena-West Helena. The Forest Service identifies it as the Great River Road and highlights views into the Mississippi and St. Francis river valleys. Between Bear Creek Lake and Storm Creek Lake, approximately fourteen miles remain gravel.
At the northern end, Marianna’s economy historically depended on agriculture, especially cotton. The community was known as Walnut Ridge until 1852, when it became Marianna.

Begin at Marianna beside the L’Anguille River, within a break in Crowley’s Ridge. The ridge-top drive passes Bear Creek Lake, at 625 acres, then the 420-acre Storm Creek Lake before reaching the Helena-West Helena end of the route.

moments.title: Marianna
moments.text: Marianna lies beside the L’Anguille River in a break in Crowley’s Ridge, with an economy historically tied to cotton. Its transport history includes a small baseball footnote: the 1909 Marianna Brickeys took their name from the city’s street-bricking work the year before. In 1915, the Missouri Pacific Railroad built a brick depot for passenger and freight service during a statewide expansion. The depot’s long, rectangular form has a tile roof and a projecting booth on the track side for the telegrapher. A matching projection on the opposite side balances the telegrapher’s booth.

moments.title: Bear Creek Lake
moments.text: Bear Creek Lake covers 625 acres, the larger of the byway’s two named lakes. Its recreation area marks one end of the gravel section of Forest Service Road 1900 that runs between the two lakes.

moments.title: Storm Creek Lake
moments.text: Storm Creek Lake covers 420 acres along the St. Francis Scenic Byway. Its recreation area marks the other end of the gravel stretch from Bear Creek Lake, on a route connecting Marianna with Helena-West Helena.

practical: Bear Creek Lake: Approximately fourteen miles of Forest Service Road 1900 remain gravel between Bear Creek Lake and Storm Creek Lake recreation areas. (checked 2026-10-11)
